parsed_output.evidence:
Root cause / sink: FilenameUtils.doNormalize(String, char, boolean) at src/main/java/org/apache/commons/io/FilenameUtils.java:348-442, driven by FilenameUtils.getPrefixLength(String) at lines 633-687. Trust boundary: any untrusted, externally-supplied path string that a caller passes into FilenameUtils.normalize()/normalizeNoEndSeparator() expecting it to either fully resolve ".." segments or return null when the path would escape above its root (this is the method's documented contract, verified interactively: normalize("/../secret.txt") -> null, normalize("//../secret.txt") -> "//../secret.txt" unchanged, on the unpatched tree).

Concretely: getPrefixLength() treats any path beginning with two separators (lines 674-682) as a Windows UNC prefix "\\\\server\\", computing the prefix length as `indexOf(separator, 2) + 1` with no validation of the "server name" substring. When that substring is literally ".." (e.g. "//../foo"), the prefix absorbs the traversal token entirely (prefix=5 for "//../foo"). doNormalize's double-dot-collapse loop (lines 405-430) only begins scanning at `prefix + 2`, so the ".." that was swallowed into the prefix is never evaluated by the "no parent segment -> return null" logic that correctly fires for "/../foo" (prefix=1, dot-dot loop starts at 3, immediately trips the `i == prefix + 2` early-return-null branch at line 409-411). The result is silently passed through unresolved and non-null.

Every trace in the alert is downstream of this same defect, and a complete fix must guard ALL of them:
1. FilenameUtils.doNormalize/getPrefixLength itself (root cause) — the direct sink exercised by this PoV via FilenameUtils.normalize(String).
2. FilenameUtils.normalize(String, boolean) (line 241-244) and normalizeNoEndSeparator(String) / normalizeNoEndSeparator(String, boolean) (lines 288-337) — all route through the same doNormalize/getPrefixLength pair and inherit the identical bypass.
3. FileSystemUtils.freeSpaceUnix / freeSpaceWindows / freeSpaceOS (traces at lines 147-148, 178-179, 209-210, 274, 282) — call FilenameUtils.normalize(path) (line 304) on the caller-supplied `path` argument and then splice the (possibly mis-normalized, still-traversal-bearing) result directly into a `cmdAttribs` String[] (lines 313/316) that is handed to `openProcess`/`Runtime.exec` (lines 398-573) as a literal argument to `df`/`dir` — i.e. the same normalize() defect here feeds a command argument rather than a file path, so a value normalize() failed to null-out or fully resolve can carry an attacker-influenced path fragment into the spawned process's arguments.
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: On unpatched code, FilenameUtils.normalize("//../secret.txt") returns the literal string "//../secret.txt" (non-null, unmodified) instead of null, even though the semantically identical single-slash form FilenameUtils.normalize("/../secret.txt") correctly returns null per the method's own documented contract ("If the double dot has no parent path segment to work with, null is returned"). Any caller using `normalize(path) == null` as a path-traversal rejection gate is silently bypassed by this double-slash-prefixed payload. The PoV prints both results and exits 0 to signal the bypass was reproduced.
parsed_output.notes: Targeted the 4th alert trace (FilenameUtils.java lines 436→243→...→FileSystemUtils.java normalize()/cmdAttribs), specifically its root cause at FilenameUtils.doNormalize/getPrefixLength, rather than the FileSystemUtils.freeSpace* command-construction traces (traces 1-3), because: (a) all four traces share this exact same defect as their common origin — the finder's own alert note says this is fundamentally a FilenameUtils.normalize path-traversal-neutralization bug, not an OS-command-injection bug; (b) FileSystemUtils.freeSpace*/openProcess only becomes exploitable to spawn arbitrary commands under much stronger additional assumptions (attacker controls the whole `path` argument to a rarely-invoked, effectively-unmaintained deprecated API) whereas the normalize() defect is directly reachable by any caller of the public, widely-used FilenameUtils.normalize()/normalizeNoEndSeparator() API; (c) exercising normalize() directly gives a fast, deterministic, non-OS-dependent PoV (no need to shell out or depend on `df`/`dir` being present in the container) while still faithfully reproducing the documented CVE-2021-29425 behavior. Verified experimentally inside the project's Docker image: unpatched normalize("//../secret.txt") == "//../secret.txt" (bypass, PoV exits 0); after applying the equivalent upstream fix (reject "." / ".." as a UNC host-name component in getPrefixLength) normalize("//../secret.txt") == null (PoV exits 1). Confirmed the product tree was restored to its original, unmodified state (`git status`/`git diff` show no changes to src/main) after this verification — only .security-pipeline/pov/PathTraversalPOV.java was added.

parsed_output.regression_hint:
Invariant a correct fix must enforce: FilenameUtils.getPrefixLength()/doNormalize() must treat a path whose "double-separator prefix" host/server-name component is "." or ".." as invalid (matching upstream commons-io's CVE-2021-29425 fix), so that FilenameUtils.normalize("//../x") returns null, exactly as FilenameUtils.normalize("/../x") already does — i.e. normalize() must be consistent regardless of how many leading separators precede a leading ".." with no real parent segment to consume.

Known bypass variants / sibling call sites the fix must also verify (not just the one path this PoV exercises):
- Backslash form: "\\\\..\\secret.txt" (Windows separator variant of the same UNC-prefix confusion).
- Mixed separators: "//..\\secret.txt", "\\\\../secret.txt".
- Trailing content after the swallowed "..": "//../../secret.txt" currently returns null already (second ".." trips the early check) but should be re-tested after the fix to ensure no regression.
- Deeper nesting: "//../a/../../secret.txt" and other combinations that still rely on the same swallowed leading "..".
- normalizeNoEndSeparator(String) and normalizeNoEndSeparator(String, boolean) — same defect, separate public entry points, must be covered by the same fix in getPrefixLength since both delegate to doNormalize.
- FileSystemUtils.freeSpaceUnix/freeSpaceWindows/freeSpaceOS — once normalize() is fixed to return null for these payloads, confirm the callers actually reject a null return (i.e. they don't silently pass a null/garbage value into the cmdAttribs array and invoke the OS command anyway); this is a secondary check beyond the normalize() fix itself since the alert traces show the tainted `path` flowing all the way to cmdAttribs/openProcess.
parsed_output.summary: Created a compiled-and-run Java PoV that calls FilenameUtils.normalize() (the shared root cause behind every FileSystemUtils/FilenameUtils trace in the alert) directly and proves that a caller relying on the documented "normalize() returns null when a path tries to escape above the filesystem root" contract is bypassed by prefixing a traversal payload with an extra leading separator (\"//../secret.txt\" vs the correctly-rejected \"/../secret.txt\"). This is the CVE-2021-29425 class of bug.

parsed_output.patch_notes: Root cause: getPrefixLength() classified any path beginning with two separators as a UNC-style prefix, computing prefix length via indexOf(separator, 2)+1 without validating the host-name substring. When that substring was "." or "..", the traversal token was absorbed into the prefix, so doNormalize's dot-dot collapsing loop (starting at prefix+2) never evaluated it, and normalize returned the string unchanged instead of null. Fix: reject the path (return NOT_FOUND) when the host-name substring between the two leading separators and the next separator equals "." or "..". Added regression test testNormalize_rejectsDoubleSeparatorDotDotPrefix covering the PoV payload and bypass variants (backslash, mixed separators, deeper nesting, normalizeNoEndSeparator), plus confirmation that legitimate UNC paths still work.
parsed_output.risk_notes: Low risk, narrow fix. All FilenameUtils/FileSystemUtils tests pass (38/38, 28/28). Full suite has 4 pre-existing unrelated failures from running as root in the container, present before and after this change. Manually confirmed the alert PoV now reports SAFE after patch.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed CVE-2021-29425-class path traversal in FilenameUtils.getPrefixLength(): a leading double-separator (UNC-style) prefix whose host-name component is "." or ".." is now rejected, so normalize()/normalizeNoEndSeparator() correctly return null for payloads like "//../secret.txt", matching existing behavior for "/../secret.txt". Closes the root-cause defect shared by every trace in the alert.
